'''Note:''' Prefer dated primary or archived sources. Soft / secondary claims are labeled. This page does '''not''' invent unpublished Lucasfilm / Decipher contract text, and does '''not''' invent card titles or game text for unreleased prototypes.

'''Decipher and the ''Star Wars'' CCG Lucasfilm license''' covers Decipher, Inc.'s commercial license to publish the ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG), the company's documented efforts to keep or extend that license in 2000&ndash;2001, the December 2001 end of the commercial license, and the handoff into volunteer [[Players Committee]] support.

Related pages: [[Players Committee-Lucasfilm agreement]] (post-Decipher PC arrangement) &middot; [[History of the Players Committee]] &middot; [[Decipher]].

This wiki is a '''fan encyclopedia'''. It is not Decipher, Lucasfilm, or the Players Committee.

== Early license and Ranch access (context) ==

By November 1994, Decipher leadership was already meeting Lucasfilm at '''Skywalker Ranch''' as part of licensee events while pursuing a ''Star Wars'' card game (Virginia ''Pilot'' contemporaneous reporting).<ref name="vapilot1994" /> SWCCG shipped December 1995 and remained in print through Theed Palace (2001).<ref name="wp-swccg" />

'''Soft / secondary:''' later interviews and community recollections describe Decipher staff visiting Lucasfilm archives / props in connection with card development; those accounts are useful context for the closeness of the licensee relationship but are '''not''' primary proof of any particular unreleased Location card (see below).<ref name="ringer2018" /><ref name="reddit-sped" />

== Efforts to keep and extend the license ==

=== July 2000 presentation to Lucasfilm (primary excerpts) ===

In materials Decipher later posted as ''Excerpts from Decipher's July 2000 Presentation to Lucasfilm'', Chairman &amp; CEO Warren Holland framed the excerpts as ''direct quotes'' from one of many presentations to Lucasfilm executives (~18 months before the public posting), published so retailers, distributors, and players could see what Decipher had wanted to do.<ref name="pres2000" />

Documented proposal themes in those excerpts include:<ref name="pres2000" />

* '''Marketing / PR:''' Decipher argued CCGs needed to be treated as a core Lucasfilm category; listed programs Decipher said it had proposed (walk-on / set / Ranch visit sweepstakes, World Championship prize support, George Lucas signature cards, convention support, in-theater promotions, mall tours with Episode II artifacts, fast-food premiums, etc.). The Decipher page states Lucasfilm did '''not''' approve these programs for Decipher.
* '''Asks of Lucasfilm:''' treat CCGs as core; balance expectations to license performance; earlier film / set / artifact access; fewer channel restrictions; worldwide release dates; avoid over-licensing; approve special marketing; help with actor appearances and cross-promotion.
* '''Digital cards:''' Decipher argued for Lucasfilm approval of digital Star Wars CCG alongside its planned digital Star Trek CCG; the page states Lucasfilm did '''not''' approve that program for Decipher.
* '''Star Wars CCG 2nd Edition:''' a backward-compatible 2nd Edition / story-arc plan aimed at a 2001 convention-season launch; the page states Lucasfilm did '''not''' approve that program for Decipher.
* '''Conclusion:''' Decipher urged Lucasfilm not to abandon SWCCG / Young Jedi brands and cited roughly a ''quarter of a billion dollars'' of customer investment in Decipher's Star Wars CCGs. The page states Lucasfilm did '''not''' grant the license extension to Decipher.<ref name="pres2000" />

=== Public comments after the loss (secondary / period press) ===

Contemporary coverage of Holland's post-announcement remarks (ICv2 summarizing a Decipher Q&amp;A; TheForce.Net interview excerpts) attributes statements that Decipher had offered Lucasfilm more money to continue than for any prior Decipher license; that Decipher believed Hasbro / Wizards influence and younger-audience Pok&eacute;mon-style expectations mattered; that relations had been frustrating for several years; and that Decipher would continue supporting existing Star Wars game activities as a ''private citizen'' with player participation.<ref name="icv2-2002" /><ref name="tfn2001" /> Settlement / legal-dispute details Holland alluded to are '''not''' published here (he said he would not disclose terms).<ref name="tfn2001" />

Wikipedia (citing ''The Duelist'') notes a 1998 license renewal covering ''The Phantom Menace'' IP and summarizes that after negotiations Lucasfilm did not renew Decipher at end of 2001, with the trading-card license going to Wizards of the Coast.<ref name="wp-swccg" /><ref name="duelist25" />

== Research note: presentation / Ranch ''Location'' card ==

Bill's research brief asked specifically about a '''special Location card''' Decipher is said to have shown in a presentation (Skywalker Ranch or similar).

=== What is attested ===

* The July 2000 presentation excerpts explicitly list '''visits to the Ranch''' among proposed '''marketing / sweepstakes''' prizes &mdash; not as a published game card title or game text.<ref name="pres2000" />
* Period reporting places Decipher executives at Skywalker Ranch for licensee events as early as 1994.<ref name="vapilot1994" />
* Soft secondary / community sources describe Decipher archive / Ranch access during development.<ref name="ringer2018" /><ref name="reddit-sped" />

=== What was '''not''' found in this research pass ===

* No primary Decipher, Lucasfilm, GPN, TFN, BoardGameGeek, or Collecting Encyclopedia entry located that names a one-off '''Skywalker Ranch''' (or similarly titled) '''Location''' card, quotes its game text, or documents that such a Location was the physical prop shown at a license presentation.
* No stable scan / checklist entry locked here for that alleged card.

'''Soft label:''' community memory of a presentation mock-up / special Location remains '''unverified''' on cited primary pages. This wiki therefore records the research ask and the gap &mdash; it does '''not''' invent a card title or game text.

== License ends (December 2001) ==

On '''28 December 2001''', Decipher announced that Lucasfilm had ended / not extended the deal under which Decipher produced Star Wars CCG.<ref name="ann122801" /><ref name="tfn2001" /><ref name="pcabout" /> Period trade coverage states Wizards of the Coast received an exclusive multi-year worldwide trading-card license (new game, Episode II content planned for 2002).<ref name="icv2-2002" /> Decipher could no longer legally ship new SWCCG expansions; cards still in development were never released as Decipher product.<ref name="wp-swccg" />

Archived Decipher announcement pages link a Radio Free Decipher interview with Warren Holland (audio / transcript links on the 2001&ndash;2002 site) and point licensing questions to Lucas Licensing contacts; later linked PC / Reflections Gold posts appear on the same navigate cluster.<ref name="ann122801" />

== Handoff to the Players Committee ==

Unable to continue producing, marketing, or commercially supporting the game, Decipher created a volunteer '''Players' Committee''' / Player Advocate structure so fans could continue tournaments, rulings, and support.<ref name="pc1" /><ref name="pcabout" /> The January 2002 Advocate announcement (Wayback-stable June 2002 HTML commonly cited on this wiki) describes turning stewardship toward players, a Norfolk meeting, and Game Players Network assistance &mdash; detailed on [[History of the Players Committee]] and [[Players Committee advocates]].<ref name="pc1" />

Public PC About pages summarize later Virtual-card distribution limits (electronic only; no physical PC cards; no new film images; free distribution). That post-license arrangement is documented separately at [[Players Committee-Lucasfilm agreement]] &mdash; this page does '''not''' reprint unpublished contract text.<ref name="pcabout" />
